summary: Added opt-in ROCm intra-kernel timestamp reads and caller-owned timestamp recording. A real MI350X vector-add kernel produced an exact independently computed Torch result, positive per-workgroup stage durations, and separate instrumented/uninstrumented ISA. HIP-event timing measured the instrumentation overhead.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact GPU vector-add agreement with independent a+b Torch reference; 32 workgroup stage intervals were positive (88/116/128 timer ticks min/median/max); dumped ISA contains two s_memrealtime instructions, two 64-bit timestamp stores, and the explicit barrier.
Exact uninstrumented GPU vector-add agreement and unchanged zero timestamp buffer; dumped ISA contains no s_memrealtime, timestamp dwordx2 store, or profiling barrier.

Focused regression suite: 4 passed and 2 backend-optional tests skipped. Median HIP-event kernel time over 25 batches of 100 launches was 37.080 us plain and 37.088 us profiled, a 0.009 us measured delta (1.000x at printed precision).

remaining_limitations: No native C++ or LLVM source changed, so the prepared native rebuild was not applicable; validation used the prepared interpreter and pinned LLVM through the checkout's Python sources.

The s_memrealtime common device time-domain contract permits same-GPU cross-XCD comparisons, but this test could not identify or pin individual workgroups to particular XCDs, so cross-XCD placement was not independently demonstrated.
Readings from different GPUs are not a synchronized shared epoch. The timer read is not a barrier, and conversion from raw ticks to time requires an independently established device timer frequency.
Direct upstream issue retrieval was blocked by the provided GitHub credential policy; the supplied upstream snapshot and accessible mirror issue were inspected without changing credentials.
